messages:
tay: Quick sync request 3: adding a short 'Region-aware provisioning' subsection to Dedicated Provisioning. Intention: show how region_affinity, reserved_pool selection, and autoscale cooldowns interact. Want a tiny Go SDK snippet + a rollforward playbook (not just rollback). cc @riley @marco for accuracy.

riley: SGTM. can you show the pool selection logic? i.e., prefer same-region reserved pools, fallback to cross-region with comment about data residency. also call out the SLA checkpoints (post-provisioning warmup) and scale-in cooldown to avoid oscillation.

tay: sketch below. plan to include a short terraform link to ops/infra/terragrunt/provisioning as the canonical infra example.

Sequence (to paste as inline list in doc):
- User requests provisioning (tenant, model, region_affinity)
- API validates quota & policy -> 409 on quota fail
- Pool selector: prefer reserved pools in region_affinity -> else consider eligible cross-region pools (flag data-residency note)
- Attach autoscale policy (min,max,cooldown,scale_in_grace_period)
- Canary deploy to 10% of traffic, run SLA checks (p95 latency, error-rate) for warmup period
- If SLA pass -> promote and mark provisioned; if fail -> rollforward to previous stable model/pool OR scale back canary and retry per policy

marco: tiny nit: we usually prefer "rollforward" wording when trying next compatible pool or model version instead of full rollback. add example values for cooldowns and p95 thresholds.

yvonne: add a short note about eviction: eviction_grace_period and eviction_priority_label. link to eng-sre runbook for preemption thresholds. also mention isolation_label decorator used by tenancy to avoid noisy-neighbor scheduling.

Go SDK snippet (short & copy/pasteable):
```go
package main

import (
  "fmt"
  "github.com/redwood/redwood-go"
)

func main() {
  client := redwood.NewDedicatedClient("$REDWOOD_KEY")
  req := redwood.ProvisionRequest{
    TenantID: "tenant_xyz",
    Model:    "gpt-large-quant",
    RegionAffinity: "eu-central-1",
    ReservedPool:   "eu-central-1-reserved-a",
    Autoscale: redwood.AutoscaleConfig{MinReplicas:1, MaxReplicas:8, CooldownSeconds: 120, ScaleInGraceSeconds: 300},
  }
  prov, err := client.Provisionings.Create(req)
  if err != nil {
    panic(err)
  }
  fmt.Println("provision id:", prov.ID)
}
```

tay: also adding a tiny YAML autoscale example to show fields in docs:

```yaml
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 1
  max_replicas: 8
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  scale_in_grace_seconds: 300
  policy: cpu
```

riley: perfect. include example thresholds in prose: p95 latency < 250ms, error_rate < 0.5% during canary (5-10 minutes). state that these are defaults and customers can override.

marco: for the rollforward playbook, add steps for: identify failing metric, try rollforward to alternate pool in same region (if available), if not, revert traffic to previous model version, and finally open incident if capacity exhausted. include commands for CLI and SDK.

Suggested rollforward checklist (to paste as bullet list in doc):
- confirm canary failure metric (p95, errors)
- attempt rollforward: `redwood-cli provision rollforward --provision-id <id> --target-pool <pool>`
- if rollforward fails, revert traffic: `redwood-cli routing set --provision-id <id> --target-version <previous>`
- reassign tenant (SDK): `client.Provisionings.Update(tenantID, ProvisionUpdate{ReservedPool: "previous_pool"})`
- re-run smoke tests and monitor p95/error for 10m
- if still failing, escalate to eng-sre with logs + commit id + recent infra events

yvonne: also add short example for marking a pool as "drain" for maintenance: `redwood-cli pool set-state --pool <pool> --state drain` and note that draining respects eviction_grace_period.
